title: Geometric-point data for a zero-dimensional field base change
statement: Let k and k′ be algebraically closed fields and f:C→Spec k a separated finite-type scheme of dimension at most zero [def-weil-pbc-curve-setting]. In a cartesian square [def-pc-base-change] with lower map ι:Spec k′→Spec k and projection ι′:C′→C, C′→Spec k′ is again a curve of dimension at most zero. There is an equivalence b:|C′|≃|C| equal pointwise to ι′, and a family of geometric points s(c′):Spec k′→C′ [def-weil-geometric-point] with s(c′)(default)=c′. No sheaf occurs in this statement.

source.place: Degree-zero proof, point bijection and chosen geometric points; Stacks Tags 00KH, 00FV, 01JT.

proof.text: The zero-dimensional base-change point description gives a bijective projection and dimension zero, and Nullstellensatz identifies residue fields on C′ with k′. Choose the canonical residue-field point at each c′; the empty scheme gives the empty family. Transport the point description from the canonical pullback to the given cartesian square.
Separatedness and finite type are stable under base change. Together with dimension zero, these supply IsCurve f′.
